subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: Should ordinary skill publishing deprecate the client-declared source flags in favor of the server-resolved GitHub-backed workflow, or retain them as a separate explicitly unverified attribution field?
rationale: Both choices can preserve trusted provenance, but the permanent public data contract, compatibility policy, and acceptable risk of publisher-asserted repository links require maintainer intent.

options.title: Deprecate publish source flags
options.body: Reject or phase out the flags for ordinary skill publishing and document server-resolved GitHub-backed sources as the supported public provenance path.

options.title: Expose unverified attribution
options.body: Persist the declared repository, ref, commit, and path separately and label them as publisher-provided and unverified on every API and UI surface.

options.title: Verify uploaded contents
options.body: Add repository authorization and content matching before promoting an ordinary CLI publish to trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Deprecate publish source flags
recommendation.body: Reject or phase out the flags for ordinary skill publishing and document server-resolved GitHub-backed sources as the supported public provenance path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged source-sync work provides the strongest available ownership signal for the adjacent trust architecture.
